body.estimand_functional: \(S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)=\{1\}\) for \(v=u\); for \(v\ne u\) and \(g_{\mathcal G,\ell}(u)=\bot\), it equals \(\{0\}\); on the cogent-group branch it equals \(\{W_{vc}/W_{uc}:c\in L_u(W,\mathcal G,\ell)\}\cup(\{0\}\text{ if }z_u(W,\mathcal G,\ell)=1)\), with singletonness read directly from equality of these displayed values.

sampling_model.design: Population exact identification on the real generic domain of Yang et al.'s recovered mixing equivalence class, with exact rational encoding used only for the separate completion-complexity question.
sampling_model.units: The population layer is indexed by the observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\). An optional region-union remark may start from \(n\) i.i.d. observations, but no first-stage inferential construction is a contribution.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention fixes a labeled substantive variable \(u\), including a variable measured with error or a fixed singleton mleaf.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is used because the population target is a linear structural intervention effect recovered from the mixing representation.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population core takes real \(W\) as the separable identification input. Rational \(\widetilde W\) is introduced only for exact \(\operatorname{CompOpt}\) bit complexity. Construction, alignment, and computation of any confidence region for an overcomplete mixing matrix are outside scope.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Algorithm 2 enumerates all row and column choices and then retains the models with the fewest structural edges.
Theorem 3.3 gives a necessary-and-sufficient generic criterion for an observed-variable total effect when the causal graph is unknown.
Section 4 computes the observationally compatible causal-effect possibilities in latent-variable LiNGAM and gives conditions for uniqueness.
Theorem 4.3 certifies generic coefficient identification under general confounding by polynomially many maximum-flow computations.
The paper enumerates Markov-equivalent DAGs with linear delay and bounded structural change between consecutive outputs.
IDA computes possible intervention effects from local CPDAG information without enumerating every DAG in the equivalence class.

body.tldr: Yang et al. identify a real canonical linear model with simultaneous latent confounding and measurement error only generically up to a minimum-edge DOG class, and their recovery algorithm enumerates a Cartesian product of center and noise assignments. The project proves that the known observation labels induce a unique total map from every intervention label to either one cogent AOG group or a fixed singleton-mleaf branch. Its headline theorem gives every labeled pairwise total-effect image exactly as normalized entries from that intervention variable's globally feasible source columns, augmented by zero when the variable can be an mleaf, and supplies an attaining minimum model for every value. Singletonness is a transparent corollary obtained by zero checks and cross-multiplication among all admissible source columns, not an independent certificate target. The central open object is a genuine complexity dichotomy for exact rational globally constrained minimum completion under coupled downstream cancellations: either a polynomial algorithm or an exact hardness result with a nontrivial tractable restriction.

project_justification.gap: Yang et al.'s Theorem 3 identifies the real mixed model generically only up to DOG equivalence, Section 5 treats one four-node effect, and Algorithm 2 uses an exponential Cartesian loop. Salehkaleybar et al. and Tramontano et al. characterize effect ambiguity without simultaneous measurement error. No located result projects every labeled mixed-model effect through globally minimum center and noise choices or classifies the complexity of coupled rational minimum completion.
project_justification.niche: Total effects have a choice-local normalized-column representation once the observation-group map and fixed singleton-mleaf branch are explicit, even though minimum-edge feasibility of a local choice is globally coupled. This separation permits an exact algebraic image theorem over the real generic domain and concentrates computational uncertainty in one auditable exact optimization problem.
project_justification.fill: The project delivers the complete \(q+1\)-point effect image with attaining countermodels, records its singleton equality test as a direct corollary, proves a faithful plateau obstruction to greedy optimization, poses an algorithm-versus-hardness classification for rational constrained minimum completion, gives the corresponding polynomial projection reduction, and verifies the no-measurement reduction.

body.related_work: Yang, Nafea, Kiyavash, Zhang, and Ghassami (2026), Definition 2, Theorems 2--3, Algorithm 2, Proposition 6, Appendix A.2, and Appendix A.4 define the real canonical model, its label-restricted AOG recovery, and the generic DOG equivalence class used here. Their generic qualification is interpreted stratumwise: the excluded proper algebraic loci have Lebesgue measure zero in the free coefficient coordinates of each nonempty real canonical coefficient stratum, with separability imposed separately on the source laws. Their algorithm enumerates every center and noise selection, with complexity proportional to \(M_{\mathrm{Row}}M_{\mathrm{Col}}\), and Section 5 analyzes robustness only in a four-node union model. Salehkaleybar, Ghassami, Kiyavash, and Zhang (2020), Section 4, provide the closest effect-image precedent by enumerating compatible latent-variable LiNGAM parameterizations; measurement-label restrictions and mleaf center changes are absent. Tramontano, Kivva, Salehkaleybar, Drton, and Kiyavash (2024), Theorems 3.3, 3.6, 3.8, and 3.11, turn admissible mixing-column swaps into complete generic total-effect criteria and a cubic-time graphical procedure when measurement error is absent. Proposition \(\text{prop:no-measurement-reduction}\) promises equivalence on that shared real generic subclass rather than a strict improvement. Tramontano, Drton, and Etesami (2026), Theorems 3.6, 4.2, and 4.3, convert determinant ranks and nonintersecting paths into maximum-flow identification tests under a different general-confounding model; this informs a possible positive branch of the complexity question but does not optimize mixed DOG completions. Wienoebst, Luttermann, Bannach, and Liskiewicz (2023) obtain linear-delay traversal of a Markov equivalence class, which informs local update control but not a global algebraic sparsity optimum. Maathuis, Kalisch, and Buehlmann (2009) compute possible DAG effects from local CPDAG information; the mixed-DOG minimum-feasibility projection is not locally rectangular. Romano and Shaikh (2010) supply general identified-set honesty terminology for the optional external premise, not a construction of an aligned overcomplete-ICA region or a contribution of this core.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact effect image requires only the projected globally minimum pairs \(P_g(W,\mathcal G,\ell)\), but computing those pairs is not known to factor across groups. The faithful benchmark has a strict coordinate-descent trap at thirteen edges and a coupled repair reaching the twelve-edge global optimum, so scalar per-group costs, strict greedy descent, and unqualified local-switch connectivity are invalid routes. Population identification is stated for real parameters on Yang et al.'s stratumwise generic domain; rational exact input \(\widetilde W\) is used only for \(\operatorname{CompOpt}\) bit complexity, with no probability assertion on \(\mathbb Q^{p\times q}\).
body.honest_scope: The core fixes Yang et al.'s real canonical, separable, minimal, LV-SEM-ME rank-faithful class with known observation labels. Equality between the recovered minimum DOG and the full observational equivalence class is asserted only for \(\theta\in\Theta_{p,q,\ell}^{\mathrm{gen}}\), a relative Zariski-open set on each nonempty real canonical coefficient variety whose complement is Lebesgue-null in the stratum's free coefficient coordinates; separability is a separate source-law assumption. The finite projected image is exact once \(W\), \(\mathcal G(W,\ell)\), and \(\Omega^{\star}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\) are fixed. The observation-group partition, normalized reconstruction, local effect column, exact projected image, its direct singleton equality corollary, plateau certificate, conditional oracle reduction, and no-measurement reduction are theorem obligations. The exact complexity of constrained minimum completion on rational inputs is the first-class unresolved question: a valid resolution may be polynomial solvability or an exact hardness theorem coupled with a nontrivial tractable restriction. When there are no measured variables or mleaf rows, the image criterion must collapse generically to Tramontano et al.'s Theorem 3.3. Self-effects equal one, and a fixed singleton-mleaf intervention has zero off-diagonal effects. Inference construction is outside scope. As an unnumbered definitional remark only, \(\text{ass:first-stage-coverage}\) and \(W\in\mathcal C_n\) imply \(S_{vu}(W,\mathcal G(W,\ell),\ell)\subseteq\mathcal E_n(v,u)\) simultaneously for every \(u,v\in V\), so the same event has probability at least \(1-\alpha+o(1)\). This is set inclusion from the definition of the union; the core neither constructs the aligned region nor counts the transfer as a theorem or contribution.
